examples: `new Formula` stores two values and calls nothing; a program makes a formula with `Formula::of` and meets one from `Reader` with `formulas: true`, and the examples of `Formula::of` show both.
perf: `new Formula` stores two values and calls nothing; `Formula::of` builds one on every call, so its figure includes this one.
hostile: `new Formula` stores two typed read-only values and calls nothing, so a wrong value does not compile; formula text and cached values are written when the row is written, and the attack of `Formula::of` sends hostile ones.
